items.description: This historic fortification was built by the Portuguese in 1588 and later extensively fortified by the Dutch in the 17th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its blend of European architecture and South Asian traditions.

Located in Kochchikade, Colombo, this Catholic shrine is a significant place of worship dedicated to Saint Anthony of Padua. It holds deep cultural importance for the multi-religious community of the capital city.

The first open-air zoo in Sri Lanka, designed to provide a naturalistic habitat for large mammals. It offers visitors an opportunity to view lions, elephants, and other species in semi-wild conditions.
facts: First open-air zoo in Sri Lanka

items.description: Situated near the famous elephant orphanage, this open zoo focuses on showcasing native fauna in well-maintained, spacious enclosures. It promotes wildlife conservation and education for local and international visitors.

The Kalu Ganga, or Black River, is a major waterway flowing from the central hills to the Indian Ocean at Kalutara. It sustains lush rainforest ecosystems and fertile agricultural lands along its course.

Walawe Ganga is an important river originating in the central highlands and providing water for various irrigation projects. Its basin supports significant biodiversity and agricultural productivity in the southern region.
Lakegala is a distinctive pyramid-shaped rock formation located in the Knuckles Mountain Range. It is often associated with local legends and offers challenging terrain for experienced hikers.
